tasks.short: Help staff by inspecting rooms, setting tables, or laundry.

steps.what: Do the setting of tables for staff members.
Join staff members in doing laundry.

tasks.design: This is physical help. The lodging manager inspects rooms, sets tables or does laundry with the team. No system takes that work. Nothing is built.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is the help itself. There was no separate record to automate.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing makes inspecting a room, setting a table or doing laundry into a system step.
tasks.still_hard: The work is physical and stays with the people on the floor.
tasks.human_edge: The manager is there to do the work when the team is behind. A record would not be the help.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The manager still inspects rooms, sets tables or does laundry when the team needs help.

reach.learn: The help is the work itself, with no extra record required

evidence.claim: Inspecting a room, setting a table and doing laundry are physical tasks and stay with the person.

assumptions: No tool is added, so upkeep is zero. The time stays in the three steps at full remaining.
The prior classes this as human. The steps agree, with no machine share.
The workflow is the help itself. It starts when a colleague asks and ends when the room, the table or the laundry is done.
unknowns: How often the lodging manager still does this personally.
Whether a union or works rule treats this as the manager's work or as covering another role.
research_questions: How many hours a week does this assistance actually take?

already_counted.description: Inspecting rooms stays entirely in that step

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The assistance stays physical and at full time. No human labour is saved. The range sits under the central net and is not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange answering services, deliver packages, and answer questions.

steps.what: Arrange telephone answering services for closed hours.
Answer questions about eating and entertainment.

tasks.design: The lodging manager answers the telephone, arranges cover for closed hours, delivers packages and answers questions about eating and entertainment. A short list of places can sit in {DOCS} for the manager to read. The answers and the deliveries stay with the person.
tasks.previous_blocker: These are calls, a handover and a walk to a room. They were never one system.
tasks.enabler_now: A list of places can be kept. It does not answer the guest.
tasks.still_hard: The guest is on the phone or at the desk, and the package still has to be carried.
tasks.human_edge: The manager answers and delivers. A list of restaurants is not an answer to this guest.
tasks.altitude: The telephone, the deliveries and the questions stay. Arranging an answering service is slightly more repeatable and still a human call.

reach.task: Answer a guest asking where to eat
reach.learn: Give the answer yourself from the same list, and do not hand the guest to an unattended reply

evidence.claim: Answering a telephone and delivering a package stay with the person who has the guest.

assumptions: The place list, if kept, is a document the manager maintains. It is not sent to the guest automatically.
The prior classes this as human. The steps agree. The call and the delivery dominate.
Upkeep is a short review of the place list so it does not go stale. The answering arrangement itself is a call, not a new system.
The workflow is the guest contact. It ends when the call, the package or the question is dealt with.
unknowns: Whether an answering service is already contracted for the whole group.
Whether packages are delivered by a porter rather than the lodging manager.
research_questions: Who answers the telephone when the lodging manager is off the desk?

already_counted.description: Answering the telephone stays in that step

incremental.description: Review the place list so directions stay current

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Calls, deliveries and answers remain. Very little time moves. The range sits under the central net and is not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet clients to schedule conventions, banquets, and receptions.

steps.what: Meet clients about conventions banquets and receptions.
Schedule details of conventions with the clients.
Write details of the functions the clients agreed.

tasks.design: The meeting stays a meeting. The lodging manager schedules the convention, banquet or reception with the client and writes the details they agreed. {CALENDAR} holds the date. It does not plan the function.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan was the meeting. The sheet afterwards was already a short write.
tasks.enabler_now: A calendar can hold the date the client and the manager agreed. It cannot hold the plan.
tasks.still_hard: The client conversation decides the function. That does not compress.
tasks.human_edge: The manager and the client agree the function. A calendar entry is only the date.
tasks.altitude: The client meetings stay the week. Writing the agreed details is a little tidier. The plan is still made in the meeting.

reach.task: Read the function sheet before the event
reach.learn: Treat the sheet as what the client and the manager agreed, and confirm gaps with them

evidence.claim: Planning a banquet or convention with a client is a meeting and stays one.

assumptions: The function sheet stores the date, the headcount, the room and the notes the manager wrote after the client agreed. The manager produces the notes. The meeting is not recorded.
The prior classes this as human. The steps agree. The meeting is most of the time.
Upkeep is the room names on the function sheet.
The workflow starts when the client asks to meet and ends when the agreed details are written. Staffing that function is a different task.
unknowns: Whether a sales colleague, rather than the lodging manager, holds these client meetings.
Whether the function sheet is already the contract a client must sign.
research_questions: Who meets the client for a banquet booking today?

already_counted.description: Writing the agreed details is already in the closing step

incremental.description: Keep room names on the function sheet

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The client meeting and the scheduling stay. Writing the agreed details is only partly shorter. The range sits under the central net and is not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Book local tour tickets only after the guest asks.

steps.what: Hear which local tours the guest wants.
Look up tickets for local tours and attractions.
Accept the request for tickets on local tours.
Review the tickets booking for guests.

tasks.design: The lodging manager hears which tour the guest wants and accepts it. {PARTNER_PORTAL} shows ticket availability and fills the booking from that accepted request. The manager reviews the booking, and only that version is sent. Nothing is booked before the guest has asked and the manager has accepted.
tasks.previous_blocker: The manager phoned the attraction or used a portal, then wrote the same names again.
tasks.enabler_now: Availability can be read and a booking form filled from fields the manager has accepted.
tasks.still_hard: The guest's request and the manager's acceptance still have to happen first. A wrong tour is hard to undo.
tasks.human_edge: The manager accepts what the guest asked for. The portal does not choose the tour.
tasks.altitude: Looking up tickets and sending a checked booking get shorter. The manager still hears the guest and still accepts the booking before it is sent.

reach.task: Book a tour a guest asked for at the desk
reach.learn: Send only a booking a person accepted after the guest asked

evidence.claim: A ticket lookup and a booking form can be filled from a request a person has accepted. The booking is sent only after that check.

assumptions: The booking stores the tour, the date, the guest name and the count the manager accepted. The manager produces the acceptance. The lookup is a read, not a recommendation.
The send references the booking the manager reviewed. If the guest changes the tour, the previous approval does not cover the new one.
The task is labelled automate. The steps agree that the lookup and the send can be deterministic, and they disagree that the booking can be unattended.
The workflow starts when the guest asks and ends when the approved booking is sent. It does not cover refunds.
Upkeep is the tour identifiers on the partner side.
unknowns: Whether the hotel already has a tour account, or each booking is a phone call.
Whether the guest must pay before the ticket is sent, and who takes that payment.
research_questions: Is tour availability already a portal, or a telephone call to each attraction?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the ticket booking is already in that step

approvals.approved_version: ticket booking the lodging manager accepted after the guest asked

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The guest's request and the manager's acceptance remain. The lookup and the send of the checked booking are the saving. The range sits under the central net and is not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Room help, the telephone, package delivery and client meetings stay. Tour tickets are looked up and sent only after the guest has asked and the manager has accepted the booking.
reach: The desk books a tour only after a person accepts the guest's request
skills_to_grow: Accepting a ticket booking before it is sent
Keeping a place list without turning it into an unattended answer
role.ambitious_version: A tour is booked only when the guest has asked and the lodging manager has accepted that booking.
